steps.text: Beat sugar and egg yolks together in a large bowl until creamy.
Mix in cocoa powder, cornstarch, and salt until well blended.

Pour mixture into a large, heavy-bottomed saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until boiling and thickened enough to coat the back of a metal spoon, 5 to 7 minutes.
Remove from heat; stir in butter and vanilla extract. Set aside to cool slightly.
Pour mixture into prepared pastry shell; chill pie in the refrigerator until set, 2 to 4 hours.

Garnish with whipped topping. Enjoy! Indulge in this decadent chocolate cream pie recipe that makes a silky smooth pudding-like filling from scratch for a chocolate lover's dream dessert. This impressive dessert comes together in no time, and the cornstarch helps stabalize and thicken the filling with ease.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Cream Pie
raw_recipe.description: This homemade chocolate cream pie has a rich and silky smooth chocolate pudding-like filling in a buttery pie crust for a deliciously dreamy dessert!

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to make this perfect homemade chocolate cream pie. A rich chocolate base is cooked and then poured into a baked pie shell. Let the pie chill until set and then garnish the top with whipped topping and a dusting of cocoa powder or chocolate shavings.

review.reviewBody:
this has a wonderful flavor - though the first time i tried it, it wouldn't set and i just ended up with a chocolate pudding. The second time i tried it, i increased it to 4 tablespoons of corn starch and that solved the problem. I don't know if that's an altitude adjustment (i live over a mile above sea level) or if it's just a general improvement

The other adjustment i would recommend makes the pie filling absolutely heavenly. I reduced the amount of milk to 2 3/4 cups and add 1/4 cup of Bailey's Irish Cream. That made this pie the best cream pie i have ever had.

I used 4 heaping tablespoons of cornstarch, an extra egg yoke, 2 cups cream and one cup of milk. It turned out fabulous. I also added 1 tablespoon of extra strong coffee to bring out the chocolate flavor. This recipe takes a while but the flavor is so much better than boxed. I will be using this whenever I want to prepare something extra special for my family.

MICROWAVEABLE recipe. It turned out perfect. I used 4 TBSP of cornstarch instead of three & I used 2 TBSP of butter instead of one. In a large glass microwaveable bowl, combine all the ingredients from step 1 using the adjustments listed above. Microwave on high for a total of 9 minutes but remove glass bowl and stir ingredients in 3 minute intervals. Pour thickened chocolate filling into a previously baked 9” pie shell. You can add cool whip or even meringue if you would like. And there is little cleanup involved.

This was a wonderful recipe for me. I am very allergic to dairy so I had to substitute Almond Milk and Almond Milk Creamer for the Milk. I used 2 whole eggs and followed other reviewer’s recommendations to use 1/4 cup cornstarch. I decreased the sugar to 1 1/3 cup as husband is not a fan of anything too sweet. I cooked it on the stove using a whisk and it took about 6 minutes. I am soooo happy with the result! Thank you for posting this lovely chocolate cream pie!!!!

Just made this so it's still cooling. I took a couple of tips from other reviews and increased the yolk count to 4, increased the corn starch to 4 tablespoons, replaced 2 cups of the milk with heavy cream, and added a tablespoon of instant coffee. The taste is good (tasted it while it was still warm) - I didn't find it bitter like others did - but I didn't like how the chocolate cream set up. The ingredients did not combine until the mixture came to a boil so it's not as smooth in texture as I think it should be. Next time, I'm either going to use a recipe that starts with a custard base or I'm going to tweak this so that I'm starting with a custard base (heating liquid ingredients and adding them to my yokes).

Good recipe. I made some modifications to make a smoother richer pie. First I whisk egg yolks and milk in saucepan, then the dry ingredients. Much easier then fooling eith yolks and sugar. I used 1 1/2 cups of light cream to 1 1/2 cups of milk for a richer and creamier pie. Upped cornstarch to 4 Tbs . Nothing worse then cutting into a running pie. This worked great and the pie is decadent!

Turned out really yummy. Used 4 tbsp cornstarch as I read it wouldn't set for some people. Also made my own graham cracker crust and homemade whipped topping and added chocolate sprinkles -may add chocolate chips or chocolate shavings as a topping next time.

Whipped Topping recipe:
2 cups heavy whipping cream
3 tbsp sugar
1 tbsp Mexican Vanilla blend

Make sure all ingredients are cold. Whip for a few minutes on medium speed until reaches desired whipped texture.

I made this pie with some adjustments. You will need 1/4 C of cornstarch to have this pie set up properly since there is 3C of milk. I also reduced the sugar to 1C and used 75% dark coco. I also used marshmallow topping and lightly toasted it! Super yummy!

Agree with the comments about increasing cornstarch. I used 5 tablespoons of cornstarch. It came out very thick which was perfect for having a firm pie. Also added a teaspoon of espresso powder which gave it a delicious flavor, really something special!

First of all, mixing egg yolks and sugar together does not produce a liquid as shown in the picture then adding more dry ingredients does not produce liquid either as shown in the next picture. And there is no way you can boil this in 5 minutes, the cooking time needs changed to 20 minutes and the prep time needs to changed to 45 minutes! However, all that being said, it came out perfectly by adding an extra egg yolk and an extra tablespoon of cornstarch! Yay!

I was very happy with the consistency. Most pie recipes I’ve tried before have been too loose a consistency. I did decrease the sugar to 1 cup and felt it was sweet enough-more like dark chocolate. I didn’t bother getting my mixer out. I measured all dry ingredients then eggs & milk in small amounts.

This is a diner style chocolate jello pie. It’s not a true chocolate cream pie, which is more like a custard. The pie filling should have a thicker consistency than the whipped cream on top. This ends up all the same texture, all one note. Unfortunately, the recipe itself is not well written. Way too much sugar, not enough cornstarch, and not nearly enough liquid between the sugar and egg yolks to ever get anywhere “creamy.” Even with a 4th yolk, my mixture was dry and crumbly until the milk was added. It needed to be sieved after thickening because the insufficient liquid at the beginning caused the sugar and cornstarch to clump. If you like a jello chocolate pie, follow the suggestions for 4 egg yolks/ 4 tbsp corn starch. Unfortunately, subbing in 2c of cream is too much fat. YMMV!
I added just a pinch more cocoa powder to make it more chocolaty

Like many others, my pie filling didn’t look like the pictures, even when I used large egg yolks. I wanted a rich, chocolatey, creamy dessert for the family, so I kept going despite the warnings. I made a homemade crust (no frozen ones on hand) and cooked the filling on the stove for 5–7 minutes, but it still didn’t thicken. I ended up cooking it for about 15 minutes and adding extra cornstarch — that finally did the trick and it thickened nicely.Then I realized I hadn’t pre-baked the crust, so I popped the whole pie in the oven for 30 minutes hoping for the best. After chilling, the top had formed a thick, chewy layer. It wasn’t perfect, but my dad loved it — so it wasn’t a total loss! 😅
It tastes good but after cutting there was always fluid in the pie shell. Had to drain it before cutting the next piece.

Very chocolatey. I will say that it did not look like the pictures in most steps but who cares if it tastes right. I would probably make my own crust in the future - because it's definitely worth making again- because there is more pudding than a premade crust can handle.

The sugar and egg yolk ratio seems way off because it's not the creamy consistency that is said in the recipe so I struggled getting that to a good consistency. I doubled the recipe and I think it calls for a lot of sugar next time I'm going to cut that down because it tastes really sweet. Otherwise a great recipe.
Trust the instructions. It won’t look just like the pictures in the steps. Only one adjustment: double it and make two because the first one will disappear!!
Use less cocoa powder and half milk and half heavy cream Delicious 😋
Great. Very rich. A little fussy to make.
